stories.headline: Downtown's City Centre mall sold for $57.3M, with 1,500 homes planned over the old Bay store
stories.dek: Edmonton developer Westrich Pacific has bought Edmonton City Centre and plans a mixed-use complex with housing over the former Hudson's Bay space, plus new stores, entertainment and a Nordic spa.

stories.headline: Kehewin Cree Nation proposes Edmonton's first urban reserve on Blatchford land
stories.dek: The First Nation wants to buy 14 hectares of the former airport lands for $1 for housing, health and education services, a spa and a 180-room hotel. Council's executive committee takes it up next week.

photo.title: Blatchford Air Traffic Control Tower

stories.headline: Province says City of Champions signs will return to highways into Edmonton
stories.dek: Transportation Minister Devin Dreeshen says Alberta will install new welcome signs with the slogan to mark the Elks' Grey Cup win. The city's old welcome signs carrying it came down in 2015.

stories.headline: Government Centre LRT station is set to become Buffalo Crossing
stories.dek: A city naming committee voted 4-0 for the name, which recalls a historic buffalo crossing on the river. Council is expected to sign off Nov. 25, and new station artwork should be finished by the end of 2027.

stories.headline: Three downtown parkades drop to a $5 flat rate for December
stories.dek: All of December, EPark will charge a $5 flat rate on weekends and on weekday evenings from 5 p.m. at the Canada Place, City Hall and Stanley A. Milner parkades to draw holiday crowds downtown.

photo.depicts: Stanley A. Milner Library seen from Churchill Square in downtown Edmonton
photo.author: Marie D Martel
photo.title: Stanley A. Milner Library from Churchill Square, Edmonton, 2026

stories.headline: High Level Bridge to close for most of 2027 for urgent storm repairs
stories.dek: Landslides and erosion from 2026's record summer rain mean the 113-year-old bridge will close from spring to late fall 2027. Its planned rehabilitation will happen at the same time. Detours are not yet set.

photo.depicts: Edmonton's High Level Bridge viewed from the base of the Walterdale Bridge
photo.author: Chris Woodrich
photo.title: High Level Bridge, Edmonton, Alberta, 2026-09-27 02

stories.headline: City proposes 4.9% property tax hike for 2027 in its new four-year budget
stories.dek: The draft 2027-30 plan would add about $200 to the average homeowner's bill. It includes a $6.3-billion capital budget with $100 million to widen Parsons Road, 215 Street and 41 Avenue.

photo.depicts: Edmonton City Hall and its memorial fountain
photo.author: D. Benjamin Miller
photo.title: Edmonton City Hall and Memorial Fountain, June 6, 2024

stories.headline: Alberta bill would let the province remove city bike lanes, and Edmonton is pushing back
stories.dek: Bill 43 would ban new bike lanes that restrict car traffic, let the province remove some existing ones at city expense and add provincial oversight of LRT plans. Mayor Andrew Knack called it dangerous.

photo.depicts: Bike lane on 102 Avenue in Edmonton
photo.author: Mack Male from Edmonton, AB, Canada
photo.title: 102 Avenue Bike Lane

stories.headline: Lower speed limits on parts of Jasper Avenue and Gateway Boulevard move a step closer
stories.dek: Edmonton's urban planning committee backed cutting limits from 50 to 40 km/h on busy roads in or near business districts, including parts of 107 Avenue and 124 Street. City council still has to approve it.

photo.depicts: Jasper Avenue westbound through downtown Edmonton
photo.author: TagaSanPedroAko
photo.title: Jasper Avenue Westbound, Downtown Edmonton 10-17-2022

stories.headline: Urgent care centres are coming, but south Edmonton still wants its hospital
stories.dek: Alberta set aside $39 million to buy land and plan nine urgent care centres, two in Edmonton. Councillors say the south side still needs a hospital, and the Heritage Valley hospital site sits empty.

photo.depicts: Grey Nuns Community Hospital in south Edmonton
photo.author: Johntwrl at English Wikipedia
photo.title: 2008-10-30 Grey Nuns Community Hospital

stories.headline: Two Edmonton schools tie for second in Fraser Institute's Alberta rankings
stories.dek: Mount Pleasant and Windsor Park tied for second among 699 Alberta schools, but four of the 10 lowest-ranked were also in Edmonton. A U of A education instructor calls test scores alone too narrow a measure.

photo.depicts: Edmonton Public Schools headquarters building
photo.author: WinterE229 WinterforceMedia
photo.title: Edmonton Public School Board Edmonton Alberta Canada 01A

stories.headline: New Edmonton building opens 40 supportive homes for homeless veterans
stories.dek: Veterans' House Canada opened its second supportive housing site, a roughly $15-million building at 13015 128 Ave. NW. It has on-site staff, a library, a garden and a park for service pets.

photo.depicts: Lion sculptures at the Edmonton Cenotaph
photo.author: Chris Woodrich
photo.title: Edmonton Cenotaph, Edmonton, Alberta, 2026-09-27 03

stories.headline: St. Albert drivers can settle November parking tickets with a new toy
stories.dek: The 17th annual Toys for Tickets campaign lets drivers ticketed Nov. 15 to 30 donate a new toy worth $30 or more at the RCMP detachment instead of paying the fine.

photo.depicts: St. Albert Place civic building in St. Albert
photo.author: WinterE229 WinterforceMedia
photo.title: St Albert Place St Albert Alberta Canada 05A

stories.headline: Investor group pitches AJHL expansion team for St. Albert, pending city ice approval
stories.dek: Investors seeking a 2027 franchise presented to the league in Devon. Governors held off on a vote until St. Albert council decides on ice time at Servus Credit Union Place.

photo.depicts: Ice rink at Servus Credit Union Place in St. Albert

stories.headline: St. Albert tattoo studio hosts fundraiser for military families ahead of Remembrance Day
stories.dek: Fountainhead Tattoo owner Andi Monk, who has run the event for seven years, planned a Sunday tattoo fundraiser for Edmonton's military family resource centre, expecting higher need after the CFB Wainwright tragedy.

stories.dek: The WHL club sent two conditional 2030 bantam draft picks to Swift Current for the 18-year-old forward. He was the seventh overall bantam pick and is now on his fourth junior team.

stories.headline: Strathcona County wedding photographer earns provincial title and a Team Canada spot
stories.dek: The Professional Photographers of Canada gave RedTree Photography owner Amy Moedt its Alberta Wedding Photographer of the Year title. She will compete for Canada at the 2027 World Photographic Cup.

stories.dek: Council voted 8-1 to spend the money on 24 replacement plaques after thieves took the bronze originals from brick sign pillars in February and March. The new ones will be cheaper concrete.

stories.dek: The draft budget focuses on maintaining aging assets and building reserves. A $513,000 home would pay about $163 more a year, and a public hearing is set for Nov. 25.

photo.author: Thankyoubaby

stories.headline: Volcano-themed playground taking shape in Fort Saskatchewan's Roseburn neighbourhood
stories.dek: Volcano Park at Roseburn Park will have a custom volcano with a spiral slide, in-ground trampolines, a cable zipline and a human hamster wheel. It is expected to open in spring 2027.

stories.dek: Construction is underway on Meta's $13-billion AI data centre. A Dalhousie professor told CTV that Trump would more likely use tariff-style measures than a ban, and the premier's office says it is waiting for details.

stories.dek: The Western Canadian Baseball League voted to suspend the Energy City Cactus Rats for one season, citing slow progress on the unfinished Energy City Metro Ballpark. The owner says he disagrees.

stories.dek: Twenty-three teams played in the In Their Honour Invitational at Heavy Metal Place, set up by a foundation Const. Brett Ryan's family created after the Edmonton officer was killed on duty in 2023.

stories.dek: Owner Jon Harringa hopes to switch on his Christmas Vacation tribute at 64 Briarwood Pt. around Dec. 2, with a new rooftop setup adding roughly 4,000 lights.

stories.dek: The WestView Health Foundation is raising $5.1 million so the Stony Plain hospital can scan patients locally instead of sending over 200 a month elsewhere. The province expects the scanner running in 2028.

stories.dek: The free parade rolls along 5th Avenue at 6 p.m. Sunday, with a craft fair, free Santa photos and crafts at City Centre Mall earlier in the day.

stories.dek: An Avison Young report found Nisku added almost 220,000 square feet of occupied commercial space in the third quarter, as Leduc County's 11.11 mill rate draws firms away from Edmonton.

stories.dek: Backed by a $30-million Canada Infrastructure Bank loan, the development will prepare lots for about 166 homes to help the 350 families waiting for housing. No completion date was given.

stories.dek: Owned by Enoch Cree Nation, the resort has grown from 600 to more than 1,700 machines and opened Canada's first Hell's Kitchen. An Indigenous thermal spa and indoor golf are planned.

stories.headline: Porsche driver, 23, was going 228 km/h, police at crash scene near Rogers Place say
stories.dek: No one was hurt in the single-vehicle crash, which left the front of a grey Porsche Taycan smashed in downtown Edmonton.
body: EDMONTON — A 23-year-old man was driving a Porsche at 228 km/h in Edmonton, police at the scene told YEGToday.
The grey Porsche Taycan was badly damaged in a single-vehicle crash near Rogers Place downtown. No one was hurt, according to police and firefighters at the scene.
The front of the car took the worst of it. The hood was crumpled, the front bumper was partly torn off and debris was scattered across the road.

Fire crews were called to the crash. Traffic cones were set out around the car while traffic kept moving through the intersection, and bystanders watched from the sidewalk. The road was wet, with patches of snow along the curb.
It wasn't known whether charges had been laid. Edmonton police have not put out a public statement about the crash, and YEGToday will update this story if they do.
unknowns: Whether the driver has been charged.
Where the car was going 228 km/h, and how that speed was measured.
Exactly when the crash happened and at which intersection.
stories.howReported: A YEGToday reporter was at the crash scene and spoke with police officers and firefighters there. The driver's age and speed come from what officers at the scene said; Edmonton police haven't released a statement yet. We'll update this story as we learn more.

stories.dek: Chief Warren Driechel told CBC's Edmonton AM the funding formula nets only about 53 new staff, 22 of them officers, and that one phase of an extortion probe cost an extra $1 million.

stories.dek: The CompStat system, piloted in northwest Edmonton and used citywide since February, flags hot spots and repeat offenders early; violent crime is down nearly 11 per cent so far this year, the commission heard.
